papers.title: O3 Increment from Prescribed Burns: Implications for Air Quality and Public Health in the Southeastern United States
papers.abstract: Abstract Prescribed fire (PF) is extensively practiced across the southeastern United States (US) to maintain fire-adapted ecosystems and reduce wildfire risk. However, PF emits substantial quantities of ozone (O3) precursors that can elevate ground-level O3 through photochemical reactions. This study quantified PF contributions to ambient O3 and associated premature mortality across 12 southeastern US states from 2013 to 2021 using the Community Multiscale Air Quality (CMAQ) model at 12-km resolution. Model results were calibrated through data fusion with surface observations, and sensitivity to spatial resolution was examined with a nested 4-km simulation over Georgia. At 12-km resolution, contribution from PFs to daily maximum 8-h average O3 (MDA8 O3) concentrations averaged to 0.34 ± 0.12 ppb across the region, accounting for ∼0.9% of ambient levels. The PF contribution to daily maximum 1-h average O3 (MDA1 O3) averaged to 0.46 ± 0.18 ppb or ∼1.1% of ambient MDA1 O3. At state level, highest annual average PF-MDA8 O3 (0.59 ± 0.14 ppb) and PF-MDA1 O3 (0.84 ± 0.22 ppb) were estimated in Georgia. Seasonal peaks (January–April) coincided with higher burning activity, with PF-MDA1 O3 exceeding 1.0 ppb in Georgia, Alabama, Florida, and South Carolina. During the nine-year period, PF-related MDA8 O3 exposure (short-term + long-term) associated 8925 (95% CI: 6273–11,567) premature all-cause deaths, with 62% linked to long-term exposure. Florida (2618), Georgia (1465), and North Carolina (910) experienced the highest absolute mortality burdens. The 4-km resolution model performed better than the 12-km model in estimating MDA8 O3 concentrations. In Georgia, the 4-km simulation estimated approximately 10% lower PF-MDA8 O3 concentrations and, consequently, approximately 10% fewer PF-MDA8 O3-attributable premature deaths than the 12-km simulation. These findings highlight the regional health relevance of PF-related O3 and underscore the need to integrate air-quality and public-health considerations into future PF management, particularly under climate-driven increases in fire activity.

papers.title: Fire history and atmospheric drying jointly control forest reburn severity
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Wildfire activity is increasing across western United States forests, leading to more frequent reburns, or areas that burn multiple times within short intervals (approximately two decades). Prior fire can reduce subsequent burn severity through fuel limitation, but this effect is not consistent across landscapes or climate conditions. Understanding when reburns burn less severely and when they do not is critical for predicting future fire behavior and informing management. Here, we evaluated how reburn severity varies with fire history, time since fire, and atmospheric drying across reburn events in 23 EPA Level III ecoregions in the western U.S. Results Using 755 small and large forested reburn events from 2001–2024 and hierarchical Bayesian models of modeled burn severity (Composite Burn Index, CBI, range 0–3), we found that predicted severity was about 15% higher in previously unburned areas than in reburned areas. However, this effect was structured by interactions between fuel history and atmospheric drying (vapor pressure deficit, VPD). Within reburned areas, reburn severity increased with time since fire and atmospheric drying, with both effects depending on initial fire severity. Predicted severity ranged from ~0.6 CBI under low VPD and shorter intervals to ~1.7 CBI under high VPD and longer intervals of the observed time range. Atmospheric drying had a stronger effect following low-severity initial fires, whereas time since fire had a stronger effect following higher-severity initial fires, indicating a shift from climate-mediated to fuel-mediated controls. Across ecoregions, these interactions reveal multiple pathways to elevated reburn severity, with interval effects strongest in more productive systems and weaker in drier interior regions. Conclusions Reburn severity is governed by interacting effects of fire history, time since fire, and atmospheric drying, rather than prior fire alone. While prior fire often reduces subsequent burn severity, this buffering effect weakens over time and under extreme fire weather. The moderating effect of prior fire therefore diminishes over time and is contingent on environmental conditions. Strategies that rely on recent fire, such as managed wildfire or prescribed burning, to reduce future severity may provide short-term benefits but are unlikely to remain reliable as fire weather becomes increasingly warm and dry.

papers.title: Climate and Wildfire Regimes Shape Tree Community Composition and Carbon Storage Across Elevation Gradients in Miombo Woodlands
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding how climate and wildfire regimes influence biodiversity and carbon (C) storage is critical for predicting the resilience of tropical woodlands under climate change. We investigated the effects of precipitation, temperature, and wildfires on stand structure, tree species richness, floristic composition, and C stocks along a 0–1500‐m elevational gradient in miombo woodlands of Chimanimani National Park, Mozambique. Seventy‐two plots were established across the gradient, and structural equation modeling was used to quantify the effects of climate, fire, and biodiversity on woodland structure and C storage. Precipitation increased with elevation and was the principal climatic driver of basal area and above‐ and below‐ground C stocks, whereas temperature had the strongest effect on species richness (SR). Fire intensity reduced basal area and live tree and litter C stocks, while fire frequency increased stem density but decreased SR. SR exerted strong positive direct effects on stand structure and tree C stocks. Floristic composition differed markedly among elevation zones, with species turnover accounting for most of the observed β‐diversity. Brachystegia microphylla and Julbernardia globiflora exhibited broad climatic tolerances and consistently contributed the largest proportion of tree C across the gradient, underscoring their importance for conservation and restoration. These findings indicate that continued warming, declining precipitation, and intensified wildfires are likely to reduce biodiversity, alter species composition, simplify woodland structure, and diminish C sequestration capacity. Conservation strategies should integrate biodiversity protection with climate‐ and fire‐adapted management to enhance the long‐term resilience and C storage of miombo ecosystems.

papers.title: Global warming and the Pacific Decadal Oscillation drive seasonally varying increases in extreme fire weather over the southwestern US
papers.abstract: Wildfire activity has increased across the western United States (US), with evidence linking these trends to anthropogenic climate forcing. Here, we analyze the frequency, intensity, and drivers of fire weather extremes in the southwestern US over the past 83 years. These extremes exhibit strong seasonality: wintertime changes align with long-term warming trends, while summertime variations are dominated by decadal fluctuations modulated by the Pacific Decadal Oscillation (PDO). Fire risk has increased steadily during December–May, outside the traditional fire season, primarily due to rising temperatures and declining relative humidity (RH). In contrast, summertime fire risk, largely governed by humidity, follows a roughly V-shaped trajectory, decreasing from 1940-1980 and then rising from 1981-2022, in close alignment with decadal shifts in the PDO. Although Earth system models reliably capture temperature-related changes, they underestimate interdecadal variability in humidity, manifested by a weak representation of the observed PDO–RH relationship and low-RH extremes in summer. Wildfire risk in the western United States increases during winter and spring in response to global warming, while summer fire weather extremes follow the variation of the Pacific Decadal Oscillation, as revealed by analysis based on long-term reanalysis.

papers.title: Suppression-induced fuel accumulation can amplify extreme fire seasons in Iberia
papers.abstract: Abstract Recent extreme fire seasons in Europe highlight the need to understand what drives this escalation and how fuel accumulation, weather variability and suppression interact to shape it. We analyse May–October burned area across mainland Iberia during 2003–2025 and identify a bimodal distribution, with ordinary seasons separated from four extreme years exceeding 4,000~km$^2$. Seasonal totals in these extreme years are dominated by a small number of large, spatially clustered fire events, motivating an examination of how extreme seasons emerge when suppression capacity is exceeded. A conceptual stochastic model combining fuel accumulation, weather variability and suppression reproduces this bimodal structure, with suppression acting as a perturbation to the balance between fuel accumulation and fire-driven fuel removal. Storyline simulations indicate that strong suppression produces low-fire seasons but allows fuel to accumulate, setting the stage for occasional extreme seasons when containment capacity is exceeded. In a scenario with doubled fuel accumulation, potentially associated with landscape abandonment and greater fuel continuity, the simulated frequency of high-fire seasons increases from 12\% to 36\%, while the 90th percentile of seasonal burned area rises from 4,684 to 10,092~km$^2$. Stronger suppression can substantially reduces the frequency of high-fire seasons but has a smaller effect on their severity. These results indicate that fuel accumulation, reinforced by strong suppression practices, shapes extreme fire regimes. Fuel management and suppression must therefore be considered together to limit both the occurrence and severity of extreme fire seasons.

papers.title: Social imaginaries on wildfires, burning practices, and fire management in two Colombian national newspapers: tensions between risk, illegality, and ecological function
papers.abstract: Introduction This article analyzes the construction of social imaginaries about the application of fire in two Colombian national newspapers, El Tiempo and El Espectador , based on three key concepts understood as distinct discursive categories: fire use and management, burning practices, and wildfires. Methodology A mixed-methods approach is adopted, combining artificial intelligence tools with qualitative analysis. The quantitative phase employs a BETO model to classify the evaluative framing of fire, while the qualitative phase utilizes a discursive analysis. The corpus consists of 504 items published in El Tiempo and El Espectador between 2020 and 2025. Results The findings show that, in the coverage of both newspapers, the application of fire is primarily represented as a problematic practice, associated with risk, illegality, and destruction. This trend is quantified by the predominance of negative valuations within the corpus. Based on the automatic classification of text fragments, 71% present a negative valuation, compared to 29% neutral. Specifically, “burning practices” concentrate 87.5% negative valuations and 12.5% neutral, while “wildfires” record 68% negative and 32% neutral, with no positive valuations identified in the manually annotated sample. In contrast, “fire use and management” has marginal visibility in the corpus, with only 24 news items; their manual classification as complete news items, reported separately because of its different unit and procedure, shows that 15 (62%) were positive and 9 (38%) negative, despite the potential of this concept to recognize ecological and territorial functions. Discussion These findings suggest that terminological distribution may contribute to consolidating interpretive frameworks that reduce the complexity of the phenomenon. Consequently, the analyzed coverage tends to leave the ecological and cultural dimensions of fire in the background, which may limit the legitimacy of integrated management approaches in environmental governance.

papers.title: Large-scale drivers of compounding hot and dry events in three breadbasket regions
papers.abstract: Abstract. Compound hot and dry events cause damage to ecosystems and society. While these events have been widely studied individually, their co-ocurrence and the associated large-scale atmospheric drivers remain less understood. Here, we use reanalysis products and observational data to identify compound hot and dry events in the historical period from 1960 to 2020. We analyze the large-scale circulation patterns associated with compound occurrence of hot and dry events when they affect large portions of three breadbasket regions in the Northern Hemisphere, namely North America, Europe and the Mediterranean and eastern Asia. We find that compound hot and dry events recur throughout the historical period and are consistently linked to Rossby wave patterns and mid-tropospheric anticyclonic ridging, which trigger land-atmosphere feedbacks resulting in the reinforcement of the events. Our study highlights that the spatial extent of compound hot and dry events offers a metric for assessing regional impacts.

papers.title: Developing Resilient Water Supplies for Great Plains Native American Reservations: Rosebud Sioux Tribe (South Dakota, USA) Challenges
papers.abstract: The Rosebud Sioux Tribe of southern South Dakota provides a case of study of the challenges Native American tribes in the Great Plains region face in developing sustainable water supplies that are resilient to both droughts and long-term climate change. The Rosebud Indian Reservation has a semiarid climate with water supplies that are particularly vulnerable to natural climate variation and a drying climate. The adaptive capacity of the tribe is constrained by the reservation having one of the highest poverty rates in the United States. Non-Indian irrigators are the largest groundwater users on the reservation, but their use is beyond the tribal government’s control. The Rosebud Sioux Tribe continues to implement measures to increase the resilience of its water supply. The Rosebud Sioux Rural Water System provides potable water to the majority of the reservation’s population using multiple water sources, both surface and groundwater, which increases the resilience of the residential potable water supply to climate change. Interventions, such as deepening or replacing shallow household wells and augmenting stock ponds with groundwater, can mitigate some immediate vulnerabilities. Establishing a large herd of bison (Wolakota Buffalo Range), a species well adapted to the Great Plains climate, will result in ecological restoration, increased economic development, and better food security. However, continuous, long-term drying and associated groundwater impacts may eventually force more transformative adaptations, particularly with respect to agriculture.

In Phase 1, six plastic ovitraps placed in tropical humid forest in the foothills of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (SNSM) collected 20 eggs and 63 larvae of Trichoprosopon digitatum and 19 larvae of Limatus durhamii . They also yielded what is, to our knowledge, the first video record of egg brooding in this species: a female guarded her egg raft for at least 7 h and resumed brooding after the raft was removed and returned. Positivity did not differ among materials, but plastic and bamboo traps accumulated about three times more eggs than clay traps (rate ratios 3.09 and 3.61), whereas the attractant had no detectable effect. Egg counts showed field evidence of skip oviposition, and 19 persistent traps held 62% of all eggs. An artificial-intelligence counter (Col-Ovo) agreed with manual counts (CCC = 0.79, rising to 0.95). Larvae reared from positive traps included Ae. aegypti, Culex quinquefasciatus, Cx. (Carrollia) cf. bihaicola, Cx. (Phenacomyia) corniger and Ae. albopictus , the first evidence of this invasive vector in Santa Marta. Simple, inexpensive traps therefore detected invasive urban vectors, sylvatic potential vectors and natural predators, and documented a rarely observed behavior. Clay traps are adequate for presence–absence surveillance, plastic or bamboo traps are preferable when egg density or egg removal is the goal, and clay and bamboo offer biodegradable alternatives to plastic.

papers.title: Characterizing drinking-water facility exposure to historical wildfires in Northern Colorado
papers.abstract: Abstract Wildfire increasingly threatens forested headwater watersheds that supply drinking water to downstream communities, yet wildfire exposure is often characterized at regional scales that do not identify which historical fires are most impactful to specific intake facilities. This limitation is especially important in managed water systems where inter-basin transfers (IBTs) expand source-water footprints beyond natural watershed boundaries. Here, we developed a reproducible spatial framework to quantify historical wildfire exposure for drinking-water intakes and applied it in northern Colorado as a case study. The analysis integrated historical (1984–2024) wildfire perimeters, burn severity, subwatershed boundaries, natural hydrologic flow paths, and IBT connectivity. Across the 7,308 km² study area, 1,895 km² burned (25.9% of the landscape), at least one fire occurred in 54 of 90 watershed, and approximately 31% of total burned area was classified as high severity. Across all fire events with downstream intake relevance, fires affected drinking-water systems serving an average of 344,854 people and 4 downstream intake facilities per event. Intake-level exposure depended not only on fire size, but also on burn severity and hydrologic connectivity. Incorporating IBTs expanded the effective source-water footprint and altered the relative importance of individual subwatersheds for evaluating fire impacts on downstream intake systems. These findings improve wildfire characterization in source-water exposure assessment and support development of decision-support tools (e.g., Forests to Faucets) linking forests, water, and communities.

papers.title: Time Series Fuzzy Bayesian Logistic Regression for Wildfire Event Prediction
papers.abstract: Abstract Wildfires are among the most destructive natural hazards, posing significant threats to ecosystems, communities, infrastructure, and economies. Accurately predicting the likelihood of wildfires enhances the effectiveness of preventive actions. Wildfire data is severely imbalanced toward the non‐fire observations due to the rare nature of wildfires. The features included in wildfire data cause separation problems and encounter seasonality. The methods used to predict wildfire probabilities need to account for these data characteristics. This study proposes a new method, TS‐FBLR, for predicting wildfire event probability. This method uses time series elements and fuzzy Bayesian modeling to handle class imbalance, separation, and seasonality in wildfire data. Extensive experimentation on 16 forests across Canada, Europe, and Australia, with data from the last 12 years, shows that TS‐FBLR outperforms 11 benchmarking methods for wildfire event classification. An out‐of‐sample benchmarking on data with a 12‐month forecast horizon demonstrates that TS‐FBLR accurately handles imbalance and separation problems with unseen data, improving implementation efficiency and providing real‐time predictions of wildfire probabilities.

papers.title: Tree and neighborhood damage have distinct effects on delayed mortality after a severe hurricane
papers.abstract: Tropical forest resilience, biodiversity, and carbon sequestration depend on tree survival. Disturbance events, such as hurricanes, generate distinct forms of damage at the individual-tree and neighborhood scale, providing a unique setting to disentangle the causal contributions of mortality drivers. Leveraging post-hurricane census data for nearly 4000 trees in the Luquillo Forest Dynamics Plot, Puerto Rico, we used a causal inference framework combined with Bayesian multilevel models to estimate the effect of individual- and neighborhood-scale damage on delayed tree mortality following Hurricane Maria (2017). Individual damage effects depended on species identity and tree size. Stem break emerged as the most lethal form of damage across the community. Neighborhood damage was associated with elevated mortality following Hurricane Maria, independent of focal tree damage. This effect was strongest among large trees, consistent with disproportionately high physiological stress resulting from greater inherent metabolic demands, refoliation energy costs, and evapotranspiration following canopy recovery. Severe biomass loss (> 75% crown loss) buffered large trees from negative neighborhood effects, revealing a positive pruning effect on survival. Our study advances mechanistic understanding of delayed tree mortality, while also suggesting how mortality patterns may shift with expected increases in disturbance severity under a warming climate.

papers.title: Biodiversity and urban low-carbon development: an empirical study from Haidian District, Beijing
papers.abstract: Urban areas face the dual challenge of mitigating carbon emissions while halting biodiversity loss, yet longitudinal evidence from Asian megacities on whether biodiversity independently enhances carbon sequestration remains limited. This study examines the biodiversity–carbon relationship using a twelve-year panel dataset from Haidian District, Beijing—a highly urbanized region where green space expansion has largely reached its spatial limits. Based on a systematic monitoring network of 40 permanent quadrats across 22 subdistricts, we constructed a comprehensive Biodiversity Index (BD) integrating plant, bird, amphibian, and soil fauna diversity with ecosystem quality and ecological function indicators. Plant and bird diversity emerge as positive predictors, with amphibian diversity exhibiting context-dependent effects confined to wetland habitats. The increasing marginal contribution of biodiversity to carbon sinks over time is consistent with a "quality transition" from area-based to quality-driven greening. The findings provide longitudinal empirical evidence that biodiversity restoration is associated with low-carbon development after urbanization stabilizes. Policy implications include integrating biodiversity premiums into carbon accounting, prioritizing functional complementarity in species selection, and protecting ecological corridors that sustain trophic interactions.

papers.title: Drought in the cloud: recognizing, framing, and contesting drought as a climate risk in Dutch social media discussions
papers.abstract: Abstract Public debate plays an important role in shaping responses to climate-related hazards such as drought. While considerable attention has been given to the physical dimensions of drought, less is known about how public debate shapes societal understanding of drought. This study examines how drought became socially recognized, framed and contested on social media in the Netherlands, a country traditionally more familiar with flood than drought management. Using a combination of social network analysis and AI-assisted classification of Dutch tweets posted between 2015 and 2022, we tracked the evolution of drought-related online communities and how they discuss and frame drought. The results show a shift from discussions of drought as a distant international issue towards a national challenge following the severe Dutch drought of 2018. As drought impacts became increasingly visible, discussions expanded beyond reporting impacts to include debates on climate change, agriculture, nature conservation and water governance. Competing frames emerged around responsibility for drought impacts and competing water demands between nature and agriculture. Some communities emphasized the role of historical land and water management practices in exacerbating drought vulnerability, while several climate-sceptical communities questioned the attribution of drought to climate change. In parts of the discussion, farmers were also portrayed primarily as victims rather than contributors to the problem. Nature-related impacts consistently received attention throughout the study period, both with nature being portrayed as a victim of drought and as part of the solution to climate change. Meanwhile, the tone of the drought debate became increasingly sarcastic and less neutral over time. Our findings demonstrate how an emerging climate risk can evolve from a distant issue to a socially contested topic, involving competing interests, responsibilities and interpretations. Understanding these dynamics can help in making policymakers aware of public concerns, and potential support for drought adaptation strategies.

papers.title: Heterogeneous impacts of temperature extremes on climate attitudes and Green voting
papers.abstract: In the past decade, the public in Europe has become more concerned about climate change and expresses stronger proenvironmental policy preferences. Based on data from the European Social Survey (2012-2022, 25 countries), we show that the increased exposure to temperature extremes has contributed to the observed changes in climate change attitudes and electoral support for environmentalist policy platforms. For each additional degree of excess temperature experienced during warm spells measured over the previous 12 mo, we find that the probabilities of being worried about climate change, of feeling responsible for climate change, and of voting for Green parties and Green coalitions increase by 4.0 [CI95: 2.5, 5.5], 2.5 [CI95: 1.1, 3.9], and 2.8 [CI95: 0.9, 3.7] percentage points respectively. We also document significant heterogeneity across individuals, based on gender and education, particularly between highly educated women and low-educated men. While the latter group consistently exhibits the lowest proenvironmental attitudes and voting, it is this group that shows the strongest increases when exposed to temperature extremes, converging toward the levels of their more educated counterparts. Further regional heterogeneity analyses reveal that the effects of warm temperature extremes are smaller in less prosperous or economically disadvantaged regions, as well as in regions with greenhouse gas emission levels above the median. The findings suggest a nuanced interplay between individual factors and contextual influences in shaping climate attitudes of European citizens and their motivations or reservations toward greater climate action.

papers.title: An Agent‐Based Model for Post‐Disaster Resource Allocation Considering Dynamic Demand
papers.abstract: In the response phase of a disaster, effective and equitable resource allocation is critical for meeting the needs of affected populations and maintaining the social order in disaster-stricken areas. However, dynamic demand driven by the mobility of disaster-affected populations can substantially impact resource allocation outcomes. To consider this mobility in the resource allocation problem, in this paper, we employ an agent-based model to simulate cross-shelter movements and assess the performance of resource allocation strategies considering a gradual increase of total available resources over time. A novel resource allocation strategy is proposed, which leverages demand estimation through a machine learning (ML) method-XGBoost. We then compare this approach against two conventional strategies: uniform distribution and historical data averaging. Through case studies using real-world data of Typhoon Ragasa from Shenzhen in China and Lal-lo in the Philippines, we demonstrate that our proposed strategy comprehensively outperforms the other two in terms of effectiveness, equity and stability. In conclusion, this ML-based prediction approach offers valuable insights to support decision-makers in the formulation of resource allocation plans.

papers.title: Death and disposability: irregular migrant-farmworkers’ extraordinary exposure to traffic ‘accidents’ in Spain
papers.abstract: Abstract The seasonal circulation of agricultural workers to dispersed and sprawling sites of agrifood production renders migrant-farmworkers some of the most flexible components of agricultural infrastructures. This flexibility is made possible by the integratedness of automobiles as well as their concomitant infrastructures and cultures into everyday life. At the same time, dangerous and sometimes fatal traffic accidents involving furgonetas (vans) carrying migrant-farmworkers to and from work are often attributed to individualised and problematic behaviours, and further invisibilised by the ordinariness of automobility and traffic ‘accidents’. Drawing on twelve months of ethnographic fieldwork—including semi-structured interviews, informal conversations, and participant observation—in Murcia, Valencia, and Catalunya, this article examines the phenomenon of traffic accidents from the perspective of structural vulnerabilities. It argues that the migrant-to-farmworker pipeline for irregular migrants, combined with the cuadrilla system of labour organisation and the sprawling geographies of agrifood circuits, creates unsafe conditions for migrant-farmworkers even when they are off the clock and off the farm. Instead, migrant-farmworkers are made to assume extraordinary risks of death and injury travelling to and from work. Twenty-five years after the 2001 accident in Lorca, Murcia, in which a furgoneta carrying fourteen Ecuadorian farmworkers was struck by a train, killing twelve and leaving only two survivors, this article commemorates the lives lost and examines the ongoing legacy of this tragedy.

papers.title: Determinants of Crop Diversification in Boro Rice‐Based, Wetland Farming Systems in Bangladesh
papers.abstract: The haor landscape of Bangladesh is highly reliant on Boro rice cultivation, making farm households vulnerable to recurring floods and climate-related risks. Crop diversification can intensify agricultural resilience and reduce production risks. This study examined the pattern, extent, and determinants of crop diversification using a cross-sectional field survey performed in 2023 among 240 farm households in three purposively selected upazilas (Itna, Mithamoin, and Nikli) of Kishoreganj district. The Simpson Diversification Index (SDI), based on crop-area shares, was used to measure crop diversification, while Censored Tobit and Ordered Probit models were employed to identify its determinants. The results showed that farmers were gradually familiarizing themselves with crops such as maize, mustard, jute, chili, sweet potato, groundnut, potato, pumpkin, black gram, and various vegetables, along with Boro rice. The mean SDI was 0.22, with 58.33% of households falling within the poor diversification category (0-0.24). The Tobit model indicated that household head education, farm size, agricultural training, marketing training, and extension contact positively associated with crop diversification. In contrast, road distance, duration of waterlogging, and agro-ecological location had negative effects. The Ordered Probit results generally confirmed these associations and also revealed a positive relationship between the dependency ratio and the higher category of crop diversification. Marginal effects indicated that agricultural training, marketing training, and extension contact increased the probability of achieving excellent diversification by 6.2, 5.5, and 4.8 percentage points, respectively, while each additional kilometer from a nearby road and each additional month of waterlogging reduced this probability by 5.4 and 3.1 percentage points, respectively. These findings emphasize the importance of improving farmer training, extension services, rural infrastructure, and location-specific waterlogging control to increase crop diversification and resilience in haor farming systems. Given the purposive selection of three upazilas in Kishoreganj district, the findings should be interpreted with caution in other haor regions.

papers.title: Methodological Approaches to Analyzing the Economic Impacts of Geoclimatic Risks in Russia
papers.abstract: Global geoclimatic shifts pose substantial risks to the Russian economy, including infrastructure degradation, declining agricultural productivity, and structural challenges associated with the energy transition. The study is motivated by the need to critically evaluate existing climate-economic modeling approaches and assess their applicability to Russian conditions. The objective is to propose an ensemble framework capable of addressing structural uncertainty in climate-economic projections. Method . The research employs a systematic literature review and comparative analysis of four major model classes, examining their theoretical foundations, data requirements, and limitations, with particular attention to the compatibility of Russian statistics with international databases and the treatment of region-specific climate processes. Results . The study identifies three principal sources of distortion in standard models when applied to Russia: reliance on global mean temperature as the sole climatic predictor, which fails to capture Arctic amplification; omission of permafrost feedback mechanisms; and aggregation bias from treating Russia as a single region. The analysis reveals that integrated assessment model (IAM)-based estimates for Russia exhibit extreme variation across studies, reflecting the inadequacy of globally aggregated damage functions. The proposed ensemble strategy — combining econometric estimation, computable general equilibrium (CGE) modeling, IAM calibration, and agent-based modeling (ABM) simulation — offers a pathway for explicit accounting of structural uncertainty. Contribution . The study provides: (1) a systematic comparison of four climate-economic model classes applied to the Russian economy; (2) substantiation of the need for regionally calibrated damage functions; and (3) an ensemble methodological strategy for robust climate-policy assessments under deep uncertainty, adapted to the structural realities of the Russian economy.

papers.title: The Origins of Allergy: An Outside‐In, Bioenergetic Hypothesis
papers.abstract: Allergic disease has risen too rapidly for inherited susceptibility to explain it, and the risk variants so far reported lie in the epithelial barrier and in type-2 immunity. We propose a five-layer model in which epithelial barrier and bioenergetic dysfunction may precede and promote type-2 immune deviation rather than arise solely as its consequence, progressing from (1) barrier and bioenergetic dysfunction, with mitochondrial DNA escaping into the cytosol, through (2) danger sensing and (3) epithelial-immune communication, to (4) type-2 immune amplification and (5) a systemic layer of circulating IgE, neurogenic amplification and the atopic march, with reciprocal inflammatory feedback. Layer 1 is also the least measured: standard immune panels carry almost none of these genes, and no genome-wide association study has implicated the mitochondrial genome or its nuclear regulators. From 1856 catalogued transcriptomic series, 985 of them expression series, we drew 116 case-control cohorts from 110 series, 3776 patients and 2164 controls, with Layer 1 prespecified as 350 genes across 19 domains. Of 212 module estimates nine survived false-discovery correction: two type-2 positive controls, two cytosolic sensing and inflammasome modules, raised in oesophageal tissue (Hedges' g +1.70) and atopic skin (+1.27), and five bioenergetic modules in oesophageal tissue. In eosinophilic oesophagitis the mitochondrial clearance limb was reduced in every one of thirteen cohorts (HIF1A -1.94, BNIP3-1.98). STING1 increased in all thirteen skin cohorts that measured it while MAVS fell in ten of thirteen oesophageal cohorts, and a STING1 minus MAVS contrast separated the allergic epithelia from psoriasis, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and asthma without exception (exact p 0.029). In one series of clinically uninvolved atopic skin KEAP1 increased while NFE2L2, claudin-1 and filaggrin decreased (p < 0.001), in tissue that is not inflamed; pooled across nine series the directions largely hold without reaching significance. Broad suppression of mitochondrial programmes across allergic tissues was not supported: the phenotype is tissue-dependent, present in eosinophilic oesophagitis and atopic dermatitis, absent in nasal polyposis and established asthma and conditional in allergic rhinitis. Prospective and experimental studies must establish temporal and causal relationships.

papers.title: Climate change as a health crisis: Mental health, non-communicable diseases, and health system resilience as neglected dimensions of national adaptation plans
papers.abstract: Recent assessments including the World Health Organization COP29 special report on climate change and health (2024) the Sixth Assessment Report (AR6) by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) 2023, and the 2025 Lancet Countdown on health and climate change confirm that climate change is a present and accelerating threat to human health with wide-ranging consequences for populations and health systems worldwide. Yet, while global mitigation efforts have gained momentum including through World Health Assembly Resolution WHA75.8 (2022) and the WHO Alliance for Transformative Action on Climate and Health (ATACH), the dominant adaptation response remains narrowly focused on infectious disease and acute disaster impacts. This commentary argues that the true health toll extends far beyond these immediate threats, encompassing three dimensions that remain systematically underrepresented in general National Adaptation Plans (NAPs): the mental health consequences of climate-driven displacement; the exacerbation of non-communicable diseases through food insecurity, air pollution, and disrupted care; and the fragility of health systems under repeated climate shocks. Critically, these dimensions remain underrepresented in general NAPs, the whole-of-government instruments through which cross-sectoral climate investments are directed, even as Health National Adaptation Plans (H-NAPs) have made greater progress in addressing them. Fewer than half of countries have developed H-NAPs, and their implementation and financing remain uneven, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) where climate vulnerability is greatest. This commentary calls for urgent integration of these overlooked burdens into climate policy through a multisectoral, whole-of-society approach coupling ambitious mitigation, which delivers immediate health co-benefits through cleaner air, active transport, and sustainable diets, with adaptation strategies that explicitly address mental health, chronic disease, and health system resilience. Only by expanding climate-health policy to explicitly address mental health, chronic disease burden, and health system resilience alongside the more visible acute impacts can we build adaptation responses that are both just and effective.

papers.title: A Probabilistic Framework for Reconstructing Weather-Related Power Outage Frequency
papers.abstract: Abstract Weather-related power outage models are usually evaluated on how well they predict a select number of individual events, whereas long-term resilience planning also requires understanding of how outage frequencies are affected by climate variability and change. We develop a probabilistic framework that reconstructs weather-related outage frequency by summing calibrated daily class probabilities. It combines EAGLE-I outage observations with hydrometeorological data across all 67 Florida counties from January 2015 to September 2024. A multiclass gradient-boosted tree model separates days with no weather-related outage from those with minor (1–2 h), moderate (2–8 h), and major (at least 8 h) outages, and is evaluated by leave-one-year-out cross-validation. The predicted probabilities are well calibrated, with expected calibration errors of 0.005 or less, and summing them recovers every class total within 3%. Including static attributes in the model raises the spatial Kling–Gupta efficiency from 0.69 to 0.97 while leaving temporal skill unchanged, showing that weather controls when outages occur and local attributes control where. For nine water years, predicted and observed annual totals correlate at 0.82 across counties. Across 26 tropical cyclones, totals correlate at 0.95 for all outages and 0.85 for major outages, far exceeding a county-by-month baseline. Skill is lowest for major and summer outages, reflecting convective and restoration processes that daily county-scale predictors do not resolve. The framework offers an open and transferable route to reconstructing outage climatology and to isolating climate-driven changes in outage frequency under a stationary-grid assumption.

papers.title: EVI ‐Derived Spectral Stability of Central Chilean Sclerophyll Forests During the 2010–2025 Megadrought and a Nested 2019–2021 Hyperdrought
papers.abstract: Abstract Climate change is increasing the frequency, severity and persistence of droughts, particularly in Mediterranean‐type ecosystems, where seasonal water limitation strongly constrains forest canopy condition and ecosystem functioning. Satellite‐derived vegetation indices provide a valuable approach for assessing canopy‐level responses to drought over broad spatial and temporal scales. However, indices such as the Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI) should be interpreted as indicators of canopy greenness and spectral vegetation condition rather than as direct measurements of net primary productivity or ecological recovery. Here, we assessed EVI‐derived canopy greenness, climatic associations and spectral stability of central Chilean sclerophyll forests during the 2010–2025 megadrought and a 2019–2021 nested hyperdrought disturbance phase. We analysed sclerophyll forest sectors distributed across the current latitudinal and physiographic range of this forest type in central Chile, from coastal areas to the interior depression and Andean foothills. Annual high‐greenness EVI composites were derived from Landsat imagery using the 90th percentile of valid observations, with the 2000–2009 period used as the pre‐megadrought spectral reference condition. Extreme EVI anomalies were estimated relative to this reference period. Annual precipitation anomalies and cumulative precipitation deficit were calculated from CHIRPS Daily precipitation data using a 1981–2009 hydroclimatic baseline, while warm‐season land surface temperature was derived from Landsat surface temperature products. Climate–EVI associations were evaluated using sector‐year regression models with cluster‐robust standard errors, and EVI‐derived resistance, recovery, and resilience were quantified using bounded ecological stability metrics. Annual P90 EVI showed marked spatial heterogeneity across the study sectors. Lower EVI‐derived canopy greenness was generally observed in northern and drier sectors, whereas higher values tended to occur in more southern or locally mesic sectors. Annual EVI was positively associated with precipitation anomalies and negatively associated with warm‐season land surface temperature, with the thermal association showing the stronger effect. Extreme negative EVI anomalies were concentrated during the 2019–2021 nested hyperdrought disturbance phase, especially in northern and central sectors. Stability metrics indicated moderate to high EVI‐derived resistance across most drought‐only sectors, but recovery and resilience varied among sectors during the 2022–2025 post‐hyperdrought trajectory. Overall, our results show that central Chilean sclerophyll forests exhibited spatially heterogeneous canopy‐level spectral responses to prolonged drought and nested hyperdrought conditions. These findings do not demonstrate complete ecological recovery or ecosystem resilience in a demographic or compositional sense. Rather, they provide evidence of sector‐level EVI‐derived resistance, recovery and resilience, highlighting the usefulness and limitations of satellite‐based stability metrics for assessing drought responses in Mediterranean forest ecosystems.

papers.title: Residual error modelling for process-based flood frequency analysis
papers.abstract: Flood frequency analysis (FFA) is essential for flood risk management and infrastructure design, yet the uncertainty associated with flood quantile estimates is often poorly characterized or disregarded—especially under data-scarce conditions. Existing uncertainty quantification methods are frequently subjective, overly complex, or impractical for routine engineering use. We introduce a simulation-based uncertainty quantification framework—UQ-flood—that integrates a process-based hydrologic model, a stochastic weather generator, and a residual error model (REM). Designed for annual maxima, the REM accounts for model bias and residual variability, enabling the generation of probabilistic streamflow ensembles tailored to extreme event analysis. We apply UQ-flood to three Canadian watersheds with long streamflow records and contrasting hydroclimatic conditions. We compare its performance against traditional statistical FFA using the Generalized Extreme Value distribution and Bayesian inference. UQ-flood yields flood quantile estimates consistent with long-record statistical methods but with substantially narrower uncertainty bounds. Under short-record conditions (e.g., 30 years), UQ-flood maintains statistically consistent estimates, while statistical FFA produces wide, often impractical uncertainty intervals. Additional experiments reveal that omitting the REM introduces systematic bias in flood magnitude estimates. UQ-flood avoids parametric assumptions about flow distributions, circumvents hydrologic model biases, and is adaptable to data-limited conditions. By explicitly propagating uncertainty from hydrologic simulation to flood quantiles, UQ-flood offers a practical alternative for robust flood risk management, including applications in infrastructure design and floodplain mapping. We recommended integrating residual error models into continuous simulation frameworks to improve bias correction and uncertainty quantification in flood risk estimation.

papers.title: Co-Optimization of Network Topology and Variable Impedance Devices under Dynamic Line Ratings Using Iterative McCormick Relaxation
papers.abstract: Grid Enhancing Technologies (GETs), such as Network Topology Optimization (NTO), Dynamic Line Rating (DLR), and Variable Impedance Devices (VIDs) are increasingly deployed in power transmission grids to address congestion and improve grid utilization. However, their growing adoption necessitates coordinated operation to fully exploit their benefits. This paper presents a unified co-optimization framework that integrates NTO, DLR, and VID to alleviate congestion and minimize operational costs. NTO is modeled using a node-breaker formulation to provide enhanced switching granularity, while DLR incorporates weather-dependent parameters, including wind speed and ambient temperature, to dynamically adjust transmission limits. The resulting formulation is a mixed-integer nonlinear program due to power flow constraints with bilinear VID terms, and discrete topology decisions. To improve tractability, we propose using a McCormick relaxation approach to linearize bilinear terms. Furthermore, we propose an iterative refinement of the McCormick relaxation scheme to enhance solution accuracy. The proposed framework is validated through detailed analyses on the IEEE 118-bus system, along with additional case studies on other benchmark systems to assess scalability. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach improves solution accuracy compared to standard McCormick relaxation, achieves solution quality close to the nonlinear formulation, and maintains computational efficiency.

papers.title: On the ethics of utilizing prediction markets for forecasting hydrological catastrophe
papers.abstract: As peer-to-peer prediction markets increasingly allow real-money wagering on environmental events, public scientific agencies are being drawn into the role of financial “settlement oracles,” the designated sources of truth against which contracts resolve. The purpose of the present paper is to examine the ethical and operational risks that follow when AI-accelerated hydrologic forecasting becomes the settlement basis for such markets, with attention to flood and drought management. We develop a taxonomy of settlement oracles that distinguishes physical observations, certified records, model forecasts, official warnings, and administrative classifications, and we reframe the parallel between forecasting and market workflows as a comparison of partially analogous information systems whose prices are not calibrated probabilities. Three cases selected for maximum variation ground the analysis: a real-money contract settling on the observed crest of a fatal river flood, a federal prosecution alleging trading on classified government information, and a contract settling on a federal drought classification. Additionally, a stylized incentive model shows that the expected profit from manipulating a settlement value grows with market liquidity, and thus that thin markets deter manipulation only by accident. Applying consequentialist, deontological, and noxious-market frameworks across five modes of professional engagement, we conclude that trading by forecasters on products they produce or can influence is unethical without qualification, that agency use of market signals is at most conditionally permissible, and that the audit benefits claimed for these markets can be captured through sanctioned adversarial testing. We close with recommendations for agencies, professional societies, regulators, platforms, and affected communities.

papers.title: Decolonial Philosophy in Action: The Plumwood Mountain Landback
papers.abstract: This article narrates the decision-making and processes behind the return of a parcel of land in New South Wales, Australia, to a Local Aboriginal Land Council. The 120-hectare property, ‘Plumwood Mountain,’ was once owned by the environmental philosopher Val Plumwood. Since Val’s death in 2008, Plumwood Inc., a not-for-profit organization and committee, became custodians of Plumwood Mountain. After a complex and slow bureaucratic legal process, in September 2024, Plumwood Inc. made the Batemans Bay Local Aboriginal Land Council the new owners of Plumwood Mountain in a historic landback. This article is authored by the members of Plumwood Inc. at the time of the handover of land title and narrates our perspectives on the process. We argue that mapping our experiences as a committee undertaking a landback is valuable, since agreements that return stolen land to First Nations peoples are always undertaken within complex webs of inter-relations and within the context of a country that has a chequered history of land restitution and rights. Drawing on an ecofeminist and decolonial framework, we hope that revealing the processes of thinking and action may be useful to others working or contemplating working in this space.

papers.title: Closed-loop neuroprosthetic control through spared neural activity enables proportional foot movements after spinal cord injury

papers.abstract: Background: Ablett Grade IV tetanus from an odontogenic portal carries high mortality in resource-limited settings because of laryngospasm, autonomic instability and prolonged ventilation. Objective: To describe the cardiorespiratory course, extubation failure by the Respiratory Rate-Oxygenation (ROX) index, and post-tracheostomy liberation in an unimmunized, severely undernourished child with odontogenic Grade IV tetanus. Methods: This single-patient case report followed a boy through a 20-day hospital course within 37 days of follow-up (October 1 to November 6, 2024) at Dr. M. Djamil General Hospital, Padang, Indonesia (ethics protocol CMHC/EC/IRB/2026/0418). Oxygenation indices, the ROX index, the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) were calculated from serial records. Results: The unimmunized boy, aged 4 years 2 months, weighed 11.0 kg (weight-for-age Z-score −3.0 SD) and had rampant dental caries, 1.0 cm trismus, opisthotonus, aspiration bronchopneumonia and hypertension (130/85 mmHg). On Day 2, reflex spasms rose to 10–12 episodes/day (NLR 7.36; SII 3,946.9 × 10³/μL), followed by apneic cardiac arrest (SpO₂ 80%, PaO₂/FiO₂ 106.7 mmHg). Extubation to high-flow nasal cannula on Day 7 failed within 2 hours (SpO₂ 82%, ROX index 2.2). After meropenem for ceftriaxone-resistant Pseudomonas sp. bacteremia and elective surgical tracheostomy on Day 9, he was weaned to a T-piece within 24 to 48 hours and continuous sedatives were stopped, and enteral baclofen was started. Spasms had resolved by Day 19; decannulation was scheduled for Day 39. Conclusion: In this child, surgical tracheostomy after ROX-documented extubation failure was followed by rapid ventilator liberation and sedative de-escalation. Causation cannot be shown.
